summary:
Allwork.space argues that employers facing steep healthcare cost increases should scrutinize pharmacy spend before cutting benefits or shifting costs to employees.

Key pressures cited: a Marsh survey projects health benefit costs per employee rising 8.2% in 2027, the biggest jump since 2003, and 11% without planned cost-reduction measures. Pharmacy now represents 29.5% of total employer healthcare spend, up from 27.2% in 2024. GLP-1 medications show how concentrated that spending is: 6% of members used them in 2025 but they drove 20.3% of prescription spending, with growth expected as indications expand into cardiovascular disease, obstructive sleep apnea, chronic kidney disease, and MASH. Weight-management GLP-1 utilization alone is expected to account for one percentage point of 2027 employer health-cost growth.

The piece frames healthcare cost as a workforce problem, not just a benefits line item. Citing a National Alliance of Healthcare Purchaser Coalitions survey of 408 employers, it reports 83% say healthcare cost increases compete with wage and salary increases, 92% say costs hurt competitiveness, and 98% say health and well-being benefits matter for attraction and retention. Cost sharing through higher deductibles, premiums, and prescription costs transfers the affordability problem to employees and may deter them from using the benefit.

Recommended actions before cutting coverage: understand PBM economics including how the pharmacy benefit manager is compensated and whether rebate and specialty pricing incentives align with lowering total cost; examine full medical and pharmacy claims data to identify spend drivers; compare clinically appropriate drug-access pathways such as manufacturer programs, alternative sourcing, and direct purchasing, assessed for compliance, affordability, and continuity of care; and measure total value across cost, access, outcomes, and employee experience rather than a single contract number. The article closes by calling for clearer ownership and collaboration among HR, finance, and benefits teams.
